sentence: She came up with a brilliant solution to the problem
hint: Subject + three-word phrasal verb + object
explanation: <Come up with> significa idear o producir una idea.

sentence: The company had to lay off hundreds of workers last year
hint: Subject + had to + phrasal verb + object + time
explanation: <Lay off> significa despedir empleados, generalmente por razones económicas.

sentence: He managed to get away with cheating on the test
hint: Subject + managed to + phrasal verb + gerund
explanation: <Get away with> significa hacer algo incorrecto sin recibir castigo.

sentence: We need to crack down on illegal parking in the city centre
hint: Subject + need to + phrasal verb + object + place
explanation: <Crack down on> significa tomar medidas estrictas contra algo.

sentence: She has been putting up with his bad behaviour for too long
hint: Subject + present perfect continuous + phrasal verb + object
explanation: <Put up with> significa tolerar algo desagradable.

sentence: The detective was trying to piece together the evidence from the crime scene
hint: Subject + was trying to + phrasal verb + object + place
explanation: <Piece together> significa ir reuniendo información. Es separable: 'piece the evidence together' también es correcto.

sentence: They decided to do away with the old regulations
hint: Subject + decided to + phrasal verb + object
explanation: <Do away with> significa abolir o eliminar.

sentence: He was looking forward to starting his new job next month
hint: Subject + was + phrasal verb + to + gerund + object
explanation: <Look forward to> va seguido de un gerundio (forma en -ing).

sentence: The government plans to phase out fossil fuel subsidies by 2030
hint: Subject + plans to + phrasal verb + object + time
explanation: <Phase out> significa eliminar gradualmente. Es separable: 'phase fossil fuel subsidies out' también es correcto.

sentence: She couldn't keep up with the pace of the advanced class
hint: Subject + couldn't + phrasal verb + object
explanation: <Keep up with> significa mantener el mismo ritmo o nivel que los demás.

sentence: The manager asked us to cut back on unnecessary expenses
hint: Subject + asked + object + to + phrasal verb + object
explanation: <Cut back on> significa reducir la cantidad de algo.

sentence: He finally owned up to making the mistake in the report
hint: Subject + adverb + phrasal verb + to + gerund
explanation: <Own up to> significa admitir la responsabilidad de algo.

sentence: Two local charities teamed up with the city council on the project
hint: Subject + three-word phrasal verb + object + prepositional phrase
explanation: <Team up with> significa unir fuerzas con alguien.

sentence: The two companies met to iron out the details of the contract
hint: Subject + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: <Iron out> significa resolver los últimos detalles de un problema.

sentence: The factory plans to wind down production by the end of the year
hint: Subject + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: <Wind down> significa reducir gradualmente una actividad.

sentence: Volunteers stepped up their efforts after the storm
hint: Subject + phrasal verb (past) + object
explanation: <Step up> significa aumentar el esfuerzo. Es separable.

sentence: The firm decided to take on three new employees this month
hint: Subject + verb + infinitive + phrasal verb + object
explanation: <Take on> significa contratar o asumir una responsabilidad.

sentence: Fear of failure held her back from applying for the promotion
hint: Subject + phrasal verb (past) + object + prepositional phrase
explanation: <Hold back> significa impedir el progreso de alguien.

sentence: The bakery is branching out into online delivery this year
hint: Subject + present continuous + phrasal verb + prepositional phrase
explanation: <Branch out into> significa expandirse hacia una nueva área.

sentence: He fell behind with his rent after losing his job
hint: Subject + phrasal verb (past) + prepositional phrase
explanation: <Fall behind with> significa atrasarse en un pago u obligación.
